tools.name: get_setup_status

Each gap comes with the next step. Call it after installing, and

tools.name: list_boards
tools.description: The boards whose panels read from a project, or from any of several with `projects`. A board shows what the team already decided matters; read one with get_board.

tools.name: list_issue_occurrences
tools.description: Recent individual occurrences of one issue, newest first: when, which user and session, release, environment, page, browser and OS. Use it to spot a pattern (one browser, one release, one customer) or to pick a user or session to follow in browse_events.

tools.name: list_issues
tools.description: Error-tracking issues (errors grouped by fingerprint) for a project, or across several with `projects`, with occurrences and affected users inside the window. Default: open issues (unresolved + regressed) sorted by occurrences over the last 14 days. Follow up with get_issue for the stack trace.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List the Vinktar projects this connection can read (a project is one app or site sending events and errors), with the workspace plan and what this connection is allowed to do. Call this first when you do not know the project handle.

tools.name: query_funnel
tools.description: Conversion through an ordered sequence of events (e.g. view_pricing → start_checkout → purchase): how many entered, how many reached each step, where they dropped, how long converting took, optionally by segment.

tools.name: query_retention
tools.description: Cohort retention: users who did targetEvent in a period form a cohort, and the table shows what share of each cohort did returningEvent in each later period. Use it for "do people come back" and "did retention improve after the change".

tools.name: query_trends
tools.description: Metrics over time: event counts, unique users or sessions, the sum, average or p95 of a numeric property, optionally split by a property (one breakdown for every series, or each series by its own) and compared to the previous period. The workhorse for "how many / how much / is it growing" questions.

tools.name: run_sql
tools.description: Run a read-only VinktarQL SELECT over the project's `events` table, for anything query_trends, query_funnel and query_retention cannot express; start with those, since what they run is what a board panel should be. A ClickHouse-flavoured subset: WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY, LIMIT, DISTINCT, IN

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: add_panel, check_fix, get_alert, get_issue, list_issue_occurrences, list_issues · Private data: get_install_guide, get_issue, get_project_keys · Public sink: add_panel, create_alert, define_event, get_alert, get_project_keys, query_retention, update_board · Destructive: add_panel, create_board, define_event, delete_board, delete_panel, run_sql, update_panel, start_project.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: add_panel, check_fix, get_alert, get_issue, list_issue_occurrences, list_issues · Private data: get_install_guide, get_issue, get_project_keys · Public sink: add_panel, create_alert, define_event, get_alert, get_project_keys, query_retention, update_board · Destructive: add_panel, create_board, define_event, delete_board, delete_panel, run_sql, update_panel, start_project

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
